recipes.name: Grilled Shrimp Tacos
ingredients_raw: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
6 (8 inch) flour tortillas, heated according to package directions
1 (12 ounce) package DOLE® All Natural Southwest Salad Kit

steps.text: Combine olive oil, lime juice, peel, and cumin in small bowl. Thread shrimp onto skewers; season with salt and pepper. Brush shrimp with lime mixture. Grill until shrimp are cooked through, about 3 minutes per side, brushing occasionally with lime mixture. Roughly chop shrimp.

Combine taco ranch dressing, sour cream and shredded cheese included in the kit. Spread mixture over each tortilla; top with shrimp, salad greens and chips. Serve with favorite toppings, such as diced tomatoes, salsa, sliced olives and/or guacamole.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Shrimp Tacos
raw_recipe.description: Hot, grilled shrimp are dressed with a sauce made from Taco Ranch Dressing, and served on warmed flour tortillas.

review.reviewBody: never mind the flour tortillas. We are gluten free, so just grill the shrimp. Make a really good guacamole, Use corn tortillas crisped, and we are set. A little freshly made salsa out of tomatoes, cilantro, onions etc goes great with it too.

These were delicious! The shrimp were absolutely delicious. The cumin paired perfectly with the shrimp! I added cilantro to the shrimp marinade because it works and I have a ton of it. I grilled the shrimp on a cast iron flat grill pan. I did not use the salad mix because I have food allergies. To make the ranch sauce I used 1/3 cup sour cream, 1 tsp taco seasoning and 1 tsp dry ranch dressing mix all three together. Serve the taco s with chopped lettuce, tomato, onion and cheese. Definitely making again as it came together quickly.

These were incredible but I made a few changes. I added a crushed garlic clove to the marinade and put it and the shrimp in a bag to sit for an hour. We grilled the shrimp in a grill basket instead of skewers and they looked so pretty I decided not to chop them up. I also didn't have the salad kit so I mixed ranch dressing with a little salsa, and skipped the sour cream. We loved these, the dressing was a perfect compliment to the citrusy shrimp.

I marinated the shrimp in the lime mixture and cooked them in a skillet....I used frozen shrimp which I will NOT do next time... I'll get fresh, but they were still good just not as good as I think they could've been. The taco ranch seasoning I made by mixing the prepared Hidden Valley ranch packet with cumin, red pepper, garlic etc. So I can control the level of salt and unnecessary ingredients, but that was SO good on the tortillas...they were very fresh tasting and light...I will use more fresh shrimp next time, but overall they were very good! :-)

Delicious. I did not have the southwest salad mix, so I made my own with ranch dressing and taco seasoning. I also used the taco seasoning on the shrimp (with the lime and oil) b/c I didn't have any cumin. Grilled them in my Pampered Chef grill pan in the kitchen.

Added garlic to the marinade, and let soak for an hour before grilling. Used corn tortillas, cabbage, and a ranch avocado sauce that I found on this site, and it was delicious! I always grill my shrimp on skewers because it doesn't taste the same when I cook them in a pan. But in S.Cal we cook outdoors year round.

I combined 2 recipes together l used the sauce recipe from the spicy grilled tacos and the southwest salad mixture from this recipe. I put them on skewers and grilled them. I then cut the shrimp up slightly and made the tacos that way. They are a great hit while tailgating at Raiders games.

I served this simple recipe along with grilled onions and a Cilantro Serrano Cream Sauce found on this site. Used the lime mixture as a 15-minute marinade (along with some minced garlic), and didn't bother to chop the shrimp. No salad kit...just lettuce and tomato. A big hit with the wife and baby!

I did not follow the recipe using the Dole salad. I made the shrimp marinade. It was good and certainly acceptable but not great. I used greek yogurt, taco seasoning and ranch dressing for the sauce. 1/3 c yogurt, 1 t of each dry seasoning.
Made as recipe stated but as others did I did not use Dole salad kit. Did lettuce and tomato and made sauce from scratch (2/3rds ranch and a 1/3 peach salsa). Family loved them.

Bravo! The key to this amazing recipe is the Southwest Salad kit. We used our sous vide for the shrimp, then fast seared it. Prepping everything before hand makes it so simple to put together after chopping the shrimp.
I copied how to do the shrimp and they were VERY tasty. I noticed the recipe says nothing about “taco ranch dressing” or everything beyond that point in the directions. Didn’t matter in the end.
These were tasty and easy to make. I used lemon instead of lime as that’s what I had on hand, but otherwise made as written. Yum.
Great and easy recipe. My only change was to add avocado to the taco itself. It only enhanced what was already delishious.
My family really enjoyed this recipe and it was easy too! My grill isn't working so I used the grill pan on the stove-top, still came out great.
It was great, but I changed everything so it isn’t really about the recipe. Shrimp in tacos can’t go wronng
Amazing shrimps. Grilling them adds a bit of irresistible smoked flavor. It easily feeds a crowd. Simple and fast to make. This just became my favorite taconite choice.

Better idea to use a smaller size tortilla, such as 6 inch, or even 
4 inch. Otherwise, very good
Used chipotle ranch as the dressing, but otherwise I loved it! Added a dash more lime as well.

This is an easy go-to meal for my busy family during the week. This recipe isn’t trying to be gourmet, but it gets the job done. Easy to find ingredients on the fly with easy prep. Really tasty. Not Torchy’s tacos, but almost as fast.
